My former BJJ coach, Chuck Glass, told me a story about another school he once helped out at: they had purple belts who froze up in half-guard-top position- they suddenly couldn't advance. It was they either passed from full guard into something else, or got caught in half and had to "reset" by allowing opponent to reclaim guard- generally not something you'd want, right? Chuck couldn't understand why at first, but after months of seeing how the head instructor was training the newer students, it became clear. Half-guard transitions were demonstrated maybe twice to newer students before it was deemed they had "mastered" it.

The results of this manifested in competitions. Nobody on that team got very far into tournaments, and a few were even submitted or swept into terrible positions from half-guard-top!

My point- if you're already deep into the study of BJJ, and you've already fought from your knees and have a decent grasp of the position, what you can and can't do from it, and how to get out of it safely, then perhaps you don't need to continue training from this position.
